- Product complexity and technical knowledge
  - IT: Solutions are often complex (software, cloud, integrations, security). Salespeople must understand architecture, integrations, APIs, and be able to coordinate technical demos and proofs-of-concept.
  - Other: Many industries sell simpler, commodity products that need less technical explanation (e.g., FMCG, retail).

  - IT: Longer sales cycles (weeks to years). Requires education, pilots, POCs, and procurement/legal review.
  - Other: Shorter, transactional cycles (days to weeks), especially retail or low-cost B2C goods.

- Decision-making and stakeholders
  - IT: Multiple buyers—CIO/CTO, security, finance, end-user managers—each with different criteria. Consensus-driven buying.
  - Other: Fewer decision-makers for many B2C or SMB purchases.

- Selling style: consultative/solution vs transactional
  - IT: Solution selling — diagnose business problems, tailor architecture, build ROI/business case.
  - Other: Many sales are product-feature or price-driven.

- Role specialization and team selling
  - IT: Cross-functional teams: SDR/BDR, Account Executive, Sales Engineer (pre-sales), Customer Success/Implementation. Sales often needs technical enablement and professional services.
  - Other: Simpler role structure; one seller may handle end-to-end.

- Pricing, contracts, and legal
  - IT: Complex pricing models (per-seat, usage-based, tiered, enterprise licensing, subscriptions) and lengthy contract/negotiation cycles with SLAs and compliance clauses.
